summary: The operator asked for the Phase 5c sketch bulleted in chat and the open questions as chips. The four sketch questions were assessed: two were genuine operator decisions and two were settled from doctrine, so only two chips were raised. The operator answered both — relays ship as a default, replaceable set (works out of the box, sovereign users swap their own), and the in-person handshake bootstraps the remote channel (meeting someone exchanges relay info so the woven network is reachable remotely, which is what lets peers hold and return recovery shares; all relay traffic stays encrypted). The two doctrine-settled answers: each tapit-attest envelope rides inside a custom encrypted Nostr event (NIP-46 reserved for the app-to-wallet sign pathway), and the wallet key is reused as the Nostr identity (D-06). All recorded as D-11; the Phase 5c sketch updated from open-questions to resolved decisions. Phase 5c is now fully designed.
